name: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha

angles.text: Reverence for An'she and Mu'sha lies at the core of tauren spiritual identity, reminding young braves that life requires honoring the twin celestial lights as faithfully as the Earthmother herself.
Tauren druids look to the eternal dance of sun and moon as the primal embodiment of balance, guiding their understanding of nature's cosmic rhythms.
While shaman speak directly with the worldly spirits of earth, fire, water, and air, they pay equal homage to the celestial twins whose light sustains all living energy.
The sacred rites performed on the mesa showcase the deep, nature-revering culture that the nomadic tauren bring to their allies within the Horde.

faq.answer: An'she and Mu'sha are the sun and the moon in tauren mythology, revered as the twin eyes of the Earthmother. Unlike the spirits of earth, air, fire, and water, they do not dwell directly within the soil of Azeroth. Instead, they illuminate the world from the firmament above, with An'she offering warmth and life, while Mu'sha provides nocturnal guidance and solace.

aliases: why revere the sun and moon
faq.answer: Tauren philosophy teaches that balance is essential to all existence. While earthly spirits govern the immediate landscape, the light of An'she and Mu'sha gives vital energy, vision, and hope to all living creatures. Offering smoldering incense at high places is an act of reciprocal respect, acknowledging that mortal life cannot thrive without the continuous benevolence of both celestial bodies.
faq.q: Why do the tauren make offerings to the sun and moon?

aliases: how to find the incense shrine
faq.answer: The shrine of An'she and Mu'sha is situated in the high hills to the southeast of the mesa. It overlooks the broad plains below and lies just south of the thorny quilboar territories. Its high elevation provides a clear, unobstructed view of the open sky, making it an ideal place to lift smoke toward the heavens.
faq.q: Where is the shrine of An'she and Mu'sha located?

faq.answer: The smoldering incense acts as a physical conduit of prayer and respect. As its fragrant embers burn, the rising smoke carries the traveler's devotion directly upward into the sky toward the sun and moon. Casting the embers into the shrine fire concludes the ritual, rewarding the pilgrim with a tranquil sense of spiritual fulfillment.
faq.q: What is the significance of the smoldering incense?

faq.answer: The ritual demands vigilance, speed, and care from the pilgrim. The incense must still be smoldering when cast into the sacred fire at the shrine, meaning the journey must be completed before the embers burn out into cold ash. Furthermore, immersion in water will immediately extinguish the embers, spoiling the offering before it can reach the heights.
faq.q: Why must the incense be delivered quickly and kept dry?

aliases: are quilboar a threat to pilgrims
faq.answer: Quilboar tribes occupy heavily defended thorn dens in the hills just north of the shrine's location. While the shrine itself rests in a quiet overlook south of their grounds, travelers must be careful not to stumble into quilboar brambles, as hostile attacks could easily delay or disrupt the delicate journey.
faq.q: Do the quilboar threaten the pilgrimage to the shrine?

faq.answer: Tauren myth recognizes the moon as Mu'sha, the loving left eye of the Earthmother who gazes down upon mortal life. Other races on Azeroth, most notably the night elves, revere the same luminous white moon as the goddess Elune, but tauren tradition views her as inextricably bound to her solar twin, An'she.
faq.q: How does Mu'sha compare to other cultures' views of the moon?

sections.body: In tauren myth, the sun and the moon are known as An'she and Mu'sha, revered as the twin eyes of the Earthmother. While the elemental spirits dwell directly within the stones, winds, and waters of Azeroth, these celestial twins watch over the world from the heights of heaven. Their constant journey across the sky marks the eternal rhythm of day and night, granting warmth, guidance, and hope to all living creatures. Honoring the twins is an essential spiritual duty, teaching that balance requires reverence not only for the land beneath one's feet, but also for the light shining down from the sky.
sections.title: The Eyes of the Earthmother

sections.body: To honor the celestial twins, a pilgrim must carry smoldering incense into the southeastern hills overlooking the mesa, nestled just south of the prickly quilboar grounds. The journey is an exercise in attentiveness and speed: the fragrant embers must be delivered before they burn away to cold ash, and travelers must take care to keep them away from water along the trail. Upon reaching the elevated shrine, the pilgrim casts the embers into the sacred fire, letting the aromatic smoke carry their respect up into the sky toward the sun and moon.
sections.title: An Offering on the Heights

summary: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha is a sacred tauren pilgrimage undertaken on Red Cloud Mesa to honor the sun and moon as the celestial eyes of the Earthmother. By carrying fragile, smoldering incense to an elevated shrine in the southeastern hills, travelers show respect to the heavenly lights that bring warmth, life, and direction to the plains.
attribution: In-game quest text: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha
